proof: The single-player exclusion guard is represented correctly in metadata; the OnNewGame and PainHook paths are evaluated only for their single-player behavior.

positive_path: UIName=UI_UT_analgesia resolves to exactly 'Analgesia'.
negative_path: A missing key would not produce this display through Translator.getText; the JSON property exists once.
proof: The medical term is a display label only and is not used as the trait registry ID.

positive_path: The description's immediate mechanic—pain is suppressed regardless of injuries—matches PainHook setting Stats.PAIN=0 without modifying BodyDamage.
negative_path: The word 'permanently' is contradicted by the missing-load/migration repair: with the trait present but UT_painImmune absent, the hook returns and pain is not suppressed.
proof: Displayed copy accurately distinguishes pain sensation from injury state but overstates lifecycle persistence.

positive_path: The selected EN name and description keys exist and are nonempty.
negative_path: No non-English locale files exist in the ledger's exact translation inventory, so there is no mod-provided translation for either string.
proof: English coverage is structurally complete; multilingual coverage is absent.

positive_path: Static value is cost 12 for next-update suppression of every positive PAIN value, with three explicit exclusions and no wound/healing protection.
negative_path: Source cannot price pain immunity against injury-awareness risk, medication value, difficulty settings, or the load defect; comparative gameplay evidence is required.
proof: A balance run must declare injury mix, pain sources, co-traits, save/load path, session duration, and control character.

positive_path: PainHook adds O(1) work per live-player update: one modData lookup, one Stats reference, one Stats.get, and at most one Stats.set; it allocates no per-update table and grows persistent state by one boolean key.
negative_path: Dead players exit in centralDispatch before core handlers; missing flag exits before Stats access; PAIN=0 avoids the setter. Cost scales with player-update count, not wounds or world size.
proof: Central dispatch builds a shared tick context once for all core/trait handlers; Analgesia does not invoke lazy enemy or injury collection builders.

positive_path: Named cases assert registration, new-game flag=true, trait-absent flag=nil, PainHook changes PAIN 50->0 when flag true, and leaves PAIN 50 when flag absent.
negative_path: No test serializes/reloads modData+Stats, constructs trait-present/flag-missing load state, removes the trait while flag remains true, checks OnNewGame (player,square) order, or asserts core-handler priority/cadence.
proof: Positive and negative stat paths are directly asserted in separate UniversalTraits and UT_CORE suites.
Tests were inspected but not executed because commands/tests were forbidden.

positive_path: MockPlayer supplies trait objects, modData, Stats, and exact OnNewGame/OnPlayerUpdate handler registries; CharacterStat.PAIN has [0,100], and event fire forwards arbitrary arguments.
negative_path: makeStats.set does not clamp; OnNewGame tests fire only player rather than engine (player,square); mocks do not serialize KahluaTable/Stats, distinguish new game from load, or prove IsoPlayer.update production.
proof: Current mocks faithfully exercise the simple positive/absent-flag branches but permit signature/lifecycle mistakes the engine would expose.

positive_path: Selected UniversalTraits source/release pairs match: registry 251da2a8..., definitions 0f6f69c6..., UI 06033932..., UT_analgesia.lua 6575f8a7..., mod.info 6dc0f672.... Selected UT_CORE pairs also match: API dcd4fb67..., PainHook 048ced5b..., TickDispatch fe61d63b..., UT_CORE mod.info 1e60ee7c....

proof: Parity spans both required mods, not only the per-trait file.

positive_path: UniversalTraits mod.info requires UT_CORE and both target Build 42; LuaManager shared loader case-insensitively sorts and RunLua loads UTCore_API, PainHook, TickDispatch, and UT_analgesia from enabled mod common/version trees. Alphabetical UTCore file order makes API available before PainHook and TickDispatch available after handler registration.
negative_path: Without UT_CORE dependency/API the trait initializer can call an absent UTCore; without TickDispatch the registered core handler has no central event edge, though PainHook's fallback only applies when registerCoreHandler itself is absent.
proof: All required source and release files exist and hash-match; no explicit require statement owns these shared files.
On a changed package, full process relaunch is required because loaded Lua modules/functions persist for the session.
